instructions: Record the opponent's first exit direction from three separate pressure exchanges.
Note the lead foot and shoulder direction that announce each exit.
Choose the step and angle that closes the preferred route without crossing the feet.
progress: Verify the predicted exit and cut-off in the next ring-position round.

name: Low-Kick Steering Map (Kickboxing)
why: Study whether low kicks change the opponent's stance, weight distribution or escape direction.

mindset.intent: Use the low kick to shape movement before advancing behind the next attack.
mindset.focus: Weight settling on one leg, stance narrowing or a forced step after the kick lands or is checked.
mindset.reset: If balance is not recovered after the kick, reset the stance before applying pressure.
mindset.anchor: Kick the base, read the route.
mindset.context: Finish balanced at punching range with the opponent's next exit made predictable.

instructions: Compare the opponent's movement after inside and outside low kicks.
Identify which target shifts weight or turns their next escape most reliably.
Select the pressure step that follows that reaction while preserving guard and stance.
progress: Track whether the chosen low kick predicts the next exit during technical rounds.

name: Safe Range-Crossing (Kickboxing)
why: Find how to cross kicking range into punching range without walking onto a kick, knee or counter.

mindset.intent: Close distance behind cover, a feint or a committed opponent recovery.
mindset.focus: Their kicking-side hip, rear-hand position and weight as the athlete takes the first closing step.
mindset.reset: If the opponent stays loaded to intercept, stop outside and rebuild behind the guard.
mindset.anchor: Cross behind a reaction, never through a weapon.
mindset.context: Finish in balanced punching range with the head off the opponent's strongest return line.

instructions: Review entries from outside kick range to the first clean punching position.
Identify which feint, block or opponent kick recovery protects the crossing step.
Mark the loaded-hip or planted-knee cue that cancels the entry.
progress: Drill the safest crossing route without adding a long combination.

name: Cut-Off Combination Decision (Kickboxing)
why: Choose the opponent-specific combination that scores after the preferred ring exit is denied.

mindset.intent: Attack the guard and stance presented by the completed cut-off.
mindset.focus: Whether the expected opponent shells, pivots back, squares up or fires immediately when trapped.
mindset.reset: If the cut-off arrives late or square, cover and reclaim centre instead of forcing volume.
mindset.anchor: Complete the cut, then strike the reaction.
mindset.context: Finish outside the opponent's return line with centre still controlled.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's reaction when their primary exit is closed.
Match a shell, pivot or counter posture to one rehearsed punch-kick combination.
Define the late-cut cue that converts the attack into a defensive reset.
progress: Run the decision from a live ring cut and grade balance after the combination.

name: Low Kick After Hands (Kickboxing)
why: Identify when the expected opponent's punch defence leaves a safe low-kick finish.

mindset.intent: Kick only when the hands have fixed weight and delayed the return attack.
mindset.focus: Their checking leg, planted weight and counter hand after the selected punch sequence.
mindset.reset: If weight stays light or the counter hand is loaded, exit behind guard without the kick.
mindset.anchor: Hands fix the stance; the low kick finishes it.
mindset.context: Finish with the kicking leg recovered and head beyond the immediate counter line.

instructions: Review the expected opponent's stance response to the camp's primary hand combination.
Choose the punch beat that plants weight on the intended low-kick target.
Add the no-kick branch for a lifted checking leg or loaded counter hand.
progress: Rehearse the finish only when the opponent gives the mapped weight reaction.

name: Pressure Without Counter Exposure (Kickboxing)
why: Apply matchup pressure while denying the expected opponent's best counter lane.

mindset.intent: Advance behind a shape that protects against the known return.
mindset.focus: The opponent's shoulder, hip or lead-foot load that precedes their preferred counter.
mindset.reset: When that load appears, stop the combination, defend and step to the safe side.
mindset.anchor: Pressure closes space, not awareness.
mindset.context: Finish guarded at an angle where the known counter cannot continue cleanly.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's highest-value counter against forward movement.
Locate the earliest body cue and the range where that counter becomes live.
Build the pressure action that closes space while covering or removing its line.
progress: Grade pressure rounds on counter denial as well as forward territory.

name: First Pressure Sequence (Kickboxing)
why: Compress the opening pressure plan to one familiar ring cut and scoring response.

mindset.intent: Use the trusted entry only when the known first-exit cue appears.
mindset.focus: The opponent's rehearsed lead-foot turn toward their preferred lane.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the counter side loads; cover, hold centre and restart behind the opening feint.
mindset.anchor: See the exit, close it once.
mindset.context: Finish balanced after the trusted combination with centre still owned.

instructions: Name the single familiar exit cue retained for round one.
Visualise the practiced cut-off and one known scoring combination.
Rehearse the loaded-counter danger cue followed by the centre reset.
progress: Carry only this opening sequence into fight week.

name: Final Pressure Reset (Kickboxing)
why: Keep one familiar reset that prevents late-camp pressure from becoming square pursuit.

mindset.intent: Restore stance before the next forward step.
mindset.focus: The known posture cue of reaching, narrow feet or head passing the lead knee.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opponent pivots outside while base is lost; cover and re-square in centre.
mindset.anchor: Base restored, then advance.
mindset.context: Finish at defended striking range with both legs ready to check or kick.

instructions: Recall the single over-pressure cue seen in camp.
Pair it with the practiced stance-and-guard reset.
End on one familiar action that restarts pressure after balance returns.
progress: Use this as the final short pressure reminder.

name: Punch Counter Trigger Map (Kickboxing)
why: Identify the earliest cue and pattern in the opponent's punch entries.

mindset.intent: Select a legal punch counter before the combination reaches full speed.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot step, shoulder turn, guard opening and the first two punches of the pattern.
mindset.reset: If the pattern changes, cover and angle away instead of guessing the return.
mindset.anchor: Read the entry, counter the opening.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the final punch line with guard restored.

instructions: Rewind repeated punch entries to the first visible foot or shoulder cue.
Name the punch pattern and the defensive opening it creates.
Choose one counter and the post-counter position that avoids the remaining punches.
progress: Call the pattern correctly from the cue in three new examples.

name: Kick Counter Trigger Map (Kickboxing)
why: Recognise kick preparation early enough to defend and return in balance.

mindset.intent: Choose the defensive action from the kick line before selecting the legal counter.
mindset.focus: Hip turn, chamber, supporting-foot pivot and weight transfer before the kick releases.
mindset.reset: If the line is unclear, use the safest cover or distance defence and reset stance.
mindset.anchor: See the hip, own the recovery beat.
mindset.context: Finish in stance after the return, outside the opponent's follow-up hands.

instructions: Separate cues for low, body and head kick lines in repeated clips.
Match each clear line to check, block, withdraw or evade before naming a counter.
Select the legal return available during the opponent's kicking-leg recovery.
progress: Validate that the counter lands without delaying stance recovery.

name: Counter Range Audit (Kickboxing)
why: Learn which ranges make the athlete's preferred counters score cleanly and which make them jam or miss.

mindset.intent: Hold the distance where defence and return fit inside one balanced exchange.
mindset.focus: Opponent step depth and where their attack finishes relative to the athlete's lead foot.
mindset.reset: If distance collapses too far, tie up briefly or angle out before trying to counter.
mindset.anchor: Right counter, right distance.
mindset.context: Finish at the counter's ideal range with room to defend the next weapon.

instructions: Compare the same counter against short, correct and overextended opponent entries.
Mark where the return lands with full form and where it becomes crowded.
Choose the range adjustment used before the next counter attempt.
progress: Audit technical rounds for clean distance rather than total counter attempts.

name: Low-Kick Counter Decision (Kickboxing)
why: Build an opponent-specific answer to inside and outside low kicks.

mindset.intent: Defend or intercept according to weight placement, then score during stance recovery.
mindset.focus: Supporting-leg load, kick side and how quickly the opponent replaces their stance.
mindset.reset: If the opponent recovers square and guarded, reset instead of forcing the return.
mindset.anchor: Solve the low kick, then take the recovery.
mindset.context: Finish balanced after a check, withdrawal, intercept or counter with both feet ready.

instructions: Separate the expected opponent's inside and outside low-kick setups.
Choose check, withdraw or intercept from the athlete's weight position at release.
Match the opponent's slow or fast stance recovery to a legal counter or disciplined reset.
progress: Rehearse the decision with varied low-kick lines and require balanced finishes.

name: Body-Kick Counter Decision (Kickboxing)
why: Exploit the expected opponent's body-kick setup without surrendering body protection.

mindset.intent: Complete the chosen defence before returning into the scoring window.
mindset.focus: Their hand setup, hip line and guard position while the kicking leg travels to the body.
mindset.reset: If the kick leaves them balanced and covered, exit rather than reaching for a late return.
mindset.anchor: Protect the body; score on the landing.
mindset.context: Finish after the return at an angle beyond the opponent's follow-up punch.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's preferred hand or feint setup for the body kick.
Select the block, evade or distance response that preserves stance against that line.
Locate the return opportunity during their leg landing and define the no-window exit.
progress: Drill the defence-return-exit sequence against the matchup setup.

name: Counter-and-Angle Exit (Kickboxing)
why: Choose the exit angle that prevents the expected opponent from countering the counter.

mindset.intent: Complete the return and leave along the side their follow-up cannot track.
mindset.focus: Their rear shoulder, lead foot and preferred second attack after absorbing a counter.
mindset.reset: If the angle is blocked, cover in place briefly and exit after their follow-up finishes.
mindset.anchor: Counter once, disappear from the return line.
mindset.context: Finish outside the opponent's lead shoulder or beyond their kicking-side hip.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's immediate answer after the selected counter lands.
Map the side their feet and shoulders need to turn for that answer.
Choose the angle that forces the extra turn and the blocked-lane defensive contingency.
progress: Review whether the exit beats the opponent's second attack in live rounds.

name: First Counter Trigger (Kickboxing)
why: Retain one familiar opening cue for the trusted counter.

mindset.intent: Fire only when the rehearsed punch or kick launch signal appears.
mindset.focus: The single foot, shoulder or hip cue confirmed throughout camp.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the attack pattern changes; cover, angle out and resume reading.
mindset.anchor: One signal, one clean return.
mindset.context: Finish balanced outside the next punch or kick line.

instructions: Name the one opponent cue carried into the opening exchange.
Visualise the familiar defence, counter and finishing position.
Rehearse one changed-pattern danger cue followed by the practiced exit.
progress: Keep the final review to this trusted trigger.

name: One Trusted Kick Counter (Kickboxing)
why: Compress kick defence to one reliable counter sequence.

mindset.intent: Use the familiar response against the opponent's best-known kick.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed hip turn that identifies the selected kick line.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: stance is too heavy to defend cleanly; withdraw and restore balance.
mindset.anchor: Read the hip, defend, return, recover.
mindset.context: Finish in full stance with guard protecting the opponent's hands.

instructions: Recall the single kick line prepared most often in camp.
Pair it with the trusted defence and legal return already drilled.
Close on the heavy-stance danger cue and the familiar withdrawal reset.
progress: Use one short mental repetition and stop.

name: Kick Range Map (Kickboxing)
why: Map the exact distances for low, body and head kicks without sacrificing balance.

mindset.intent: Choose the kick whose line and recovery fit the available range.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot gap, hip reach and whether the opponent can punch during recovery.
mindset.reset: If the kick would reach only by leaning, step out and rebuild distance.
mindset.anchor: Reach with the weapon, not the posture.
mindset.context: Finish with the kicking foot recovered outside immediate punching range.

instructions: Mark the clean contact range for the athlete's primary low, body and head kicks.
Compare the opponent's nearest legal return at each distance.
Select the stance recovery needed after every kick line.
progress: Confirm range in technical work using clean form as the scoring standard.

name: Long-Weapon Range Control (Kickboxing)
why: Use the jab, front kick and long round kick to control different entry lines.

mindset.intent: Match the long weapon to the opponent's direction rather than repeating one tool.
mindset.focus: Straight entry, outside step or planted stance at the edge of range.
mindset.reset: If the opponent crosses beneath the weapon, guard and angle away before firing again.
mindset.anchor: Choose the long tool for the line.
mindset.context: Finish at range with the opponent forced to reset their feet.

instructions: Compare which long weapon stops straight movement, lateral movement and planted pressure.
Identify the recovery position each weapon leaves against punches and kicks.
Choose a simple weapon-to-entry-line rule for the next session.
progress: Track whether the chosen tool controls movement without repeated retreats.

name: Exit Lane Audit (Kickboxing)
why: Identify the exits that preserve kicking space after the athlete scores.

mindset.intent: Leave through open floor instead of backing toward the ring boundary.
mindset.focus: Opponent lead foot, boundary position and the side their shoulders can turn fastest.
mindset.reset: If both lateral lanes close, cover forward briefly and pivot out after contact.
mindset.anchor: Exit into space that keeps the weapons long.
mindset.context: Finish facing centre at the athlete's preferred kick range.

instructions: Plot the athlete's exit after each successful long-range score.
Mark whether the lane returns to centre or drifts toward the boundary.
Choose the pivot that avoids the opponent's fastest tracking side.
progress: Audit the next technical round for exits that preserve long range.

name: Intercept Forward Pressure (Kickboxing)
why: Select the matchup-specific weapon that interrupts the opponent's committed forward step.

mindset.intent: Intercept before their punching range is established, then leave the follow-up line.
mindset.focus: The expected opponent's lead-foot landing and guard shape during pressure entry.
mindset.reset: If the intercept fails to halt them, cover and angle rather than repeating at close range.
mindset.anchor: Touch the step, then take the angle.
mindset.context: Finish at long range with the opponent needing to turn before advancing again.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's primary pressure entry and identify its committed step.
Choose the jab, front kick, low kick or knee that reaches that step safely.
Add a stopped-pressure exit and a continued-pressure defensive branch.
progress: Rehearse the intercept against the opponent's actual entry rhythm.

name: Long-to-Mid Range Transition (Kickboxing)
why: Choose when the expected opponent's long-range defence makes a brief move to mid range profitable.

mindset.intent: Enter mid range only behind the reaction created by a trusted long weapon.
mindset.focus: A long guard, planted check, backward step or kick catch attempt that exposes punching range.
mindset.reset: If their hands and stance remain ready, recover long range instead of forcing the transition.
mindset.anchor: Long range creates the mid-range window.
mindset.context: Finish the punch sequence with an angle that restores kicking distance.

instructions: Review the expected opponent's defence to the athlete's primary long weapon.
Identify the reaction that safely opens a punching entry and the reaction that closes it.
Choose the short mid-range combination and exact exit back to long range.
progress: Drill the transition only on the mapped opponent reaction.

name: Kick-and-Exit Decision (Kickboxing)
why: Select the post-kick exit from the expected opponent's return pattern.

mindset.intent: Recover the kicking leg into the lane that removes their best counter.
mindset.focus: Whether they answer with straight punches, a return kick or a lateral chase.
mindset.reset: If the intended lane is occupied, cover in stance and pivot after the first return.
mindset.anchor: The kick is finished when the exit is finished.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the opponent's counter line with both feet under the hips.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's first response to the selected scoring kick.
Match straight pursuit, return kick and lateral chase to distinct exits.
Identify the blocked-lane cue that replaces movement with guarded recovery.
progress: Grade the complete kick-recovery-exit sequence rather than the kick alone.

name: First-Round Range Script (Kickboxing)
why: Carry one familiar range-establishing sequence into the opening exchange.

mindset.intent: Use the trusted long weapon and recover before gathering more information.
mindset.focus: The opponent's first step after the rehearsed range touch.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: they cross into punching range immediately; cover and take the known lateral exit.
mindset.anchor: Set range once, read once.
mindset.context: Finish in open space at the athlete's preferred kicking distance.

instructions: Name the one long weapon used to establish range.
Visualise the familiar opponent step and the trained spacing response.
Rehearse the fast-crossing danger cue followed by the practiced exit.
progress: Keep the opening script short and unchanged.

name: First Long-Range Weapon (Kickboxing)
why: Lock in the safest familiar long-range weapon for first contact.

mindset.intent: Show the trusted weapon with full balance and immediate recovery.
mindset.focus: The known stance picture that gives its cleanest legal target.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opponent loads a simultaneous counter; feint, withdraw and reset range.
mindset.anchor: First weapon, clean recovery.
mindset.context: Finish outside the opponent's immediate hands with stance restored.

instructions: Recall the single stance cue that authorises the chosen long weapon.
Pair it with the exact recovery step used throughout camp.
Close on the simultaneous-counter danger cue and familiar withdrawal.
progress: Take only this first-contact reminder into fight week.

name: Safe Tie-Up Entry (Kickboxing)
why: Identify how to enter a brief legal tie-up without absorbing clean punches, kicks or knees.

mindset.intent: Reach close range behind a guard reaction or completed opponent attack.
mindset.focus: Opponent elbows closing, kick recovery or forward posture after punching.
mindset.reset: If their posture and knees remain loaded, stay in guard and exit rather than reaching for the neck.
mindset.anchor: Earn the tie-up, act immediately.
mindset.context: Finish with one legal close-range action and prompt separation in stance.

instructions: Compare tie-up entries after blocks, punches and opponent kick recovery.
Identify which entry protects the head and arrives with hips under the torso.
Mark the loaded-knee cue that cancels contact before the hands reach.
progress: Drill entry, one action and release without prolonged holding.

name: Knee Opportunity Recognition (Kickboxing)
why: Recognise when close-range posture creates an immediate legal knee opportunity.

mindset.intent: Knee only from balanced contact and release without extending the tie-up.
mindset.focus: Opponent torso folding, elbows widening or weight settling as distance collapses.
mindset.reset: If the target line or balance is poor, frame away and reset punching range.
mindset.anchor: See the posture, knee once, release.
mindset.context: Finish separated with guard high and both feet ready.

instructions: Review brief close-range exchanges and classify the opponent's torso posture.
Identify which posture gives a legal knee line without pulling or prolonged control.
Choose the release direction that avoids their immediate punch return.
progress: Count only knees followed by prompt balanced separation.

name: Break-and-Reset Position (Kickboxing)
why: Learn where to stand after the referee break or natural release from close range.

mindset.intent: Recover guard and angle before restarting offence.
mindset.focus: Opponent lead shoulder and kicking-side hip as separation begins.
mindset.reset: If the break leaves the athlete square, take one guarded step out before attacking.
mindset.anchor: The break creates a new first exchange.
mindset.context: Finish at protected punching range with an exit lane visible.

instructions: Pause examples at the instant contact releases and mark both stances.
Identify the opponent's fastest legal return from that separation position.
Choose the guard and step that remove the return before re-entry.
progress: Review close-range rounds for clean break position, not only inside scoring.

name: Strike-to-Brief-Clinch Decision (Kickboxing)
why: Decide when the expected opponent's reaction to strikes makes a brief tie-up and knee superior to another punch.

mindset.intent: Connect only on the matchup reaction that safely closes distance.
mindset.focus: Their shell, forward fold or collision after the selected hand combination.
mindset.reset: If they pivot or remain upright with counters loaded, angle out instead of grabbing.
mindset.anchor: Strike the opening; tie up the collision.
mindset.context: Finish with one immediate legal action and balanced release.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's response to the planned close-range combination.
Assign forward fold or chest collision to the brief-clinch branch.
Assign pivot or loaded-counter posture to the striking exit branch.
progress: Rehearse the decision with immediate release after the legal close-range action.

name: Immediate Knee Opportunity (Kickboxing)
why: Exploit the expected opponent's specific posture cue for a single immediate knee.

mindset.intent: Deliver the knee on contact before the tie-up becomes static.
mindset.focus: Their elbows flare, torso bends or weight plants after the matchup's chosen entry.
mindset.reset: If posture recovers before contact, release and return to guarded striking.
mindset.anchor: Contact, posture cue, one knee.
mindset.context: Finish separated on the safe side of the opponent's rear hand.

instructions: Identify the exact entry that produces the opponent's vulnerable posture.
Choose the legal knee line available before they rebuild stance.
Define the recovered-posture cue that cancels the knee and triggers release.
progress: Drill the opportunity at full decision speed with only one knee per held contact.

name: Clinch Break Re-Entry (Kickboxing)
why: Prepare the opponent-specific scoring action after a brief clinch breaks.

mindset.intent: Re-enter only after guard and stance are restored on separation.
mindset.focus: The direction the expected opponent steps and the hand they drop while resetting.
mindset.reset: If separation leaves the athlete square, cover and take space before attacking again.
mindset.anchor: Own the reset before the re-entry.
mindset.context: Finish after one clean score at an angle, outside return fire.

instructions: Study how the expected opponent resets after referee and natural breaks.
Identify the consistent step or guard opening that creates the re-entry.
Choose one scoring action and the square-stance cue that delays it.
progress: Rehearse release, stance recovery and one re-entry as separate beats.

name: First Close-Range Cue (Kickboxing)
why: Retain one familiar cue for the first safe close-range action.

mindset.intent: Enter, score once and release on the rehearsed posture picture.
mindset.focus: The single elbow or torso cue repeatedly confirmed in camp.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opponent's knee line stays loaded; guard and exit without tie-up.
mindset.anchor: One cue, one close action, out.
mindset.context: Finish separated in stance with head protected.

instructions: Name the one posture cue carried into the fight.
Visualise the trusted entry, legal action and immediate release.
Rehearse the loaded-knee danger cue followed by the familiar exit.
progress: Keep this as a short close-range reminder.

name: Knee-and-Release Rule (Kickboxing)
why: Compress brief-clinch work to one rule-compliant knee-and-release sequence.

mindset.intent: Use the familiar knee only when balance and legal target are already present.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed body position that requires no prolonged holding or adjustment.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: grip or posture needs rebuilding; release immediately and reset guard.
mindset.anchor: Immediate knee or immediate release.
mindset.context: Finish outside close range with both feet under the hips.

instructions: Recall the single contact position used successfully in preparation.
Pair it with the one legal knee and practiced release direction.
Close on the poor-position danger cue and the known guard reset.
progress: Do not add another close-range option in fight week.

name: Range Transition Map (Kickboxing)
why: Understand the steps that connect kicking, punching and brief knee ranges.

mindset.intent: Move between striking ranges with stance ready for the next legal weapon.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot distance and opponent posture at each range boundary.
mindset.reset: If balance is lost while crossing range, guard and return to the last stable distance.
mindset.anchor: Every range change ends in stance.
mindset.context: Finish where the chosen next weapon can score without reaching.

instructions: Mark the athlete's clean kicking, punching and immediate-knee distances.
Identify the footwork or opponent reaction that safely connects each range.
Name the stable reset position when the transition closes too quickly.
progress: Call the intended range before moving through it in technical work.

name: Hands-to-Kicks Decision (Kickboxing)
why: Recognise which punch reactions leave a clean kick line.

mindset.intent: Select the kick from the opponent's guard and weight shift after the hands.
mindset.focus: Elbows pinching, guard rising, stance planting or weight moving onto one leg.
mindset.reset: If the punching exchange leaves the athlete square, exit before kicking.
mindset.anchor: Hands move the guard; feet confirm the kick.
mindset.context: Finish with the kicking leg recovered and the opponent outside punch range.

instructions: Compare opponent reactions after the athlete's jab, cross and hook patterns.
Match raised guard, closed elbows and planted weight to distinct legal kick targets.
Identify the athlete-balance cue that cancels every kick continuation.
progress: Test the punch-to-kick choice against varied guard reactions.

name: Attack or Counter Identity (Kickboxing)
why: Decide which exchanges the athlete should initiate and which should begin with a read.

mindset.intent: Use initiative at controllable range and counter when the opponent must overcommit.
mindset.focus: Who owns the lead foot, centre and first safe scoring line.
mindset.reset: When neither advantage is clear, establish range rather than forcing an identity.
mindset.anchor: Lead from control; counter from invitation.
mindset.context: Finish each exchange in the range that supports the chosen role.

instructions: Review successful attacks and counters separately across several rounds.
Identify the position that makes initiating reliable and the cue that makes waiting productive.
Write one simple rule for switching between attacker and counter striker.
progress: Use the next session to confirm the rule without increasing output.

name: Punch-to-Kick Continuation (Kickboxing)
why: Choose the matchup-specific kick created by the opponent's defence to a planned punch sequence.

mindset.intent: Kick the opening their guard and stance reaction actually presents.
mindset.focus: Their elbow position, checking leg and weight after the final planned punch.
mindset.reset: If the checking leg is ready or weight stays mobile, angle out after the hands.
mindset.anchor: Punches create the target; stance permits the kick.
mindset.context: Finish after the kick beyond the expected counter punch.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's guard and weight response to the selected punch sequence.
Map body, head and low-kick openings to the specific reactions that create them.
Add the ready-check branch that ends with a guarded angle instead.
progress: Rehearse the continuation only on its mapped reaction.

name: Kick-to-Punch Continuation (Kickboxing)
why: Exploit the expected opponent's stance recovery after the selected kick.

mindset.intent: Enter with punches only when their landing beat delays guard or foot recovery.
mindset.focus: The opponent's returning leg, hand position and step direction after absorbing or defending the kick.
mindset.reset: If they recover square and guarded, remain at kicking range and reset.
mindset.anchor: Read the landing before closing with hands.
mindset.context: Finish the punch continuation on an angle that restores kick distance.

instructions: Study how the expected opponent resets after the athlete's primary kick.
Identify the slow-stance or open-guard landing that authorises punching entry.
Define the fast-recovery cue that keeps the athlete long.
progress: Drill kick recovery, read and punch entry as three distinct beats.

name: Pressure-to-Counter Switch (Kickboxing)
why: Recognise when opponent-specific resistance makes continued pressure inferior to drawing a counter opportunity.

mindset.intent: Stop advancing once the opponent plants to fire and prepare the rehearsed return.
mindset.focus: Their retreat ending, stance loading and preferred counter-side shoulder or hip turning.
mindset.reset: If they keep escaping without setting, hold centre and resume ring cutting.
mindset.anchor: Pressure until they plant; counter when they fire.
mindset.context: Finish after the return at an angle with centre retained.

instructions: Study where the expected opponent stops retreating and chooses to counter.
Identify the plant cue and the exact weapon they prefer from it.
Build the switch from guarded pressure to one counter and a safe exit.
progress: Review whether the athlete changes role on the plant rather than after being hit.

name: A/B Opening Plan (Kickboxing)
why: Keep two familiar kickboxing openings connected by one trained opponent cue.

mindset.intent: Begin with the trusted range action and switch once only if the known response appears.
mindset.focus: The rehearsed guard or stance reaction that changes the best scoring line.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opponent crowds both options; cover and take the familiar centre exit.
mindset.anchor: A first; B on the known reaction.
mindset.context: Finish at balanced scoring range with the next defence ready.

instructions: Recall opening A and its familiar finishing position.
Name the single reaction that releases opening B.
Close on the crowding danger cue and practiced centre exit.
progress: Rehearse only these two known routes in fight week.

name: First Adaptation Rule (Kickboxing)
why: Retain one familiar rule for the first tactical adjustment.

mindset.intent: Change weapon or range only after the trained defensive reaction repeats.
mindset.focus: The single opponent response confirmed during camp.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: a one-off reaction; stay with the opening plan and reset stance.
mindset.anchor: Confirm the pattern before adapting.
mindset.context: Finish the adjustment balanced at the planned new range.

instructions: Name the one repeated reaction that authorises adaptation.
Pair it with the trusted change of weapon or distance.
Rehearse the one-off danger cue followed by the familiar opening reset.
progress: Carry the rule without adding a third option.

name: Phase Route Review (MMA)
why: See the routes that repeatedly move an exchange between striking, clinch, fence and ground.

mindset.intent: Recognise phase changes early enough to arrive organised.
mindset.focus: The contact or distance cue that ends one phase and starts the next.
mindset.reset: If the route becomes unclear, protect posture and return to the last stable position.
mindset.anchor: Know which phase is arriving.
mindset.context: Finish each transition with stance, grips or base ready for effective offence.

instructions: Label the start and end phase of five representative exchanges.
Mark the single cue that caused each transition rather than every action inside it.
Identify the route where the athlete most often arrives out of position.
progress: Review that route in the next technical session and confirm an organised arrival.

name: Opponent Reaction Scan (MMA)
why: Build a clear picture of the opponent's recurring first reactions across MMA phases.

mindset.intent: Separate reliable tendencies from one-off responses.
mindset.focus: Their first guard, footwork, clinch or get-up reaction under a familiar threat.
mindset.reset: When reactions vary, return to observation rather than inventing a fixed rule.
mindset.anchor: Repeat before you rely.
mindset.context: Finish with one confirmed tendency for each relevant phase.

instructions: Sample repeated exchanges from open space, contact and ground where available.
Record only the first reaction to the same stimulus in each sample.
Keep tendencies that recur and discard isolated actions.
progress: Confirm one retained tendency during the next scheduled technical review.

name: Safe Reset Map (MMA)
why: Define safe resets for lost striking, clinch and ground positions.

mindset.intent: Return to structure before attempting to regain offence.
mindset.focus: The first posture, grip or base failure that makes continuation unsafe.
mindset.reset: Use the phase-specific reset: re-square standing, pummel in contact or rebuild frames underneath.
mindset.anchor: Structure is the route back to offence.
mindset.context: Finish in a known defensive position with vision and base restored.

instructions: Choose one common loss of structure in each phase relevant to the athlete.
Name the smallest reliable reset that restores safety in that phase.
Identify the familiar action used only after the reset is complete.
progress: Track whether technical rounds restore structure before restarting offence.

name: Second-Phase Decision (MMA)
why: Prepare the next decision after the matchup's most likely phase transition.

mindset.intent: Make the second action from the expected opponent's recovery position.
mindset.focus: Their posture immediately after the planned strike, clinch break, takedown or stand-up.
mindset.reset: If the recovery differs from the studied picture, stabilise and reassess before continuing.
mindset.anchor: Read the landing of the transition.
mindset.context: Finish with effective offence from the first stable position in phase two.

instructions: Select the transition most likely to define the matchup.
Study the expected opponent's first recovery action after that transition.
Assign one continuation and one unfamiliar-reaction reset.
progress: Rehearse the second decision from the realistic transition, not a static start.

name: Danger Route Denial (MMA)
why: Deny the expected opponent's most damaging route between phases.

mindset.intent: Remove the route's enabling position before counterattacking.
mindset.focus: The setup, foot position or grip that starts their highest-risk sequence.
mindset.reset: If denial arrives late, protect the threatened position and exit the sequence safely.
mindset.anchor: Stop the route at its first gate.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the opponent's preferred transition with position intact.

instructions: Trace the opponent's danger sequence backward from its effective finish.
Identify the earliest visible gate where the route can be denied reliably.
Choose the denial and the late-read emergency response as separate decisions.
progress: Review whether training stops the route at the gate rather than surviving its finish.

name: Effective Offence Check (MMA)
why: Judge whether the matchup plan converts position into meaningful MMA offence.

mindset.intent: Keep routes that create impact, advancement or credible finishing threats.
mindset.focus: What happens immediately after winning range, fence, top or back position.
mindset.reset: If a position stays static, advance, attack or reset rather than counting empty control.
mindset.anchor: Position is useful when offence follows.
mindset.context: Finish each planned route with a clear scoring or fight-ending action.

instructions: Review the athlete's three most likely advantageous positions in the matchup.
Name the strike, submission threat or positional advance available from each.
Remove any route whose only outcome is holding without productive continuation.
progress: Evaluate the next simulation by effective outcomes after position is won.

name: Opening Phase Cue (MMA)
why: Retain one familiar cue that identifies the likely opening phase.

mindset.intent: Begin in the trained response as soon as the known picture appears.
mindset.focus: The opponent's first stance, distance or posture signal from preparation.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the opening picture changes; protect stance and reset to centre.
mindset.anchor: Read the phase, then act once.
mindset.context: Finish the opening exchange in a stable, familiar position.

instructions: Name the single opening cue retained from camp.
Pair it with the one familiar response already rehearsed.
Close on the changed-picture danger cue and the known centre reset.
progress: Use this as a brief opening reminder only.

name: Trusted Reset Cue (MMA)
why: Carry one known reset for the moment the first MMA exchange loses structure.

mindset.intent: Interrupt disorder before trying to reclaim offence.
mindset.focus: The familiar sign of lost base, posture or inside position.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: continuing from the broken position; return immediately to the trained safe structure.
mindset.anchor: Structure before the restart.
mindset.context: Finish re-square, framed or based in the phase-appropriate safe position.

instructions: Recall the single loss-of-structure cue used throughout camp.
Visualise the one familiar positional reset attached to it.
Name the action that must wait until structure is restored.
progress: Keep the final review to this reset and no new analysis.

name: Range Reaction Review (kickboxing)
why: See how the opponent reacts at kicking, punching and immediate-knee distances.

mindset.intent: Choose a simple range rule from repeated reactions.
mindset.focus: Their first step, guard movement or hip load when each range is entered.
mindset.reset: If no reaction repeats, return to balanced observation range.
mindset.anchor: Range reveals the likely weapon.
mindset.context: Finish with one reliable cue for each relevant striking distance.

instructions: Sample the opponent at long, mid and brief close range.
Record only the first reaction at each distance.
Keep the reactions that recur and attach one safe response to each.
progress: Confirm one range reaction during the next scheduled technical session.

name: Opponent Rhythm Scan (kickboxing)
why: Identify the opponent's recurring attack and pause rhythm.

mindset.intent: Find the beat where a legal score can land without trading blindly.
mindset.focus: The count between their entry, combination end and stance recovery.
mindset.reset: When cadence changes, defend and resume counting from a safe distance.
mindset.anchor: Hear the pause before using it.
mindset.context: Finish the response before the opponent's next attack beat begins.

instructions: Count the opponent's first three complete attacking sequences.
Mark where they pause, reset feet or repeat the same tempo.
Choose one scoring action that fits the most reliable open beat.
progress: Test the timing against varied pace without chasing the pause.

name: Balanced Reset Map (kickboxing)
why: Define the safest stance reset after punches, kicks and close-range breaks.

mindset.intent: Recover balance before choosing the next scoring action.
mindset.focus: Head over hips, foot width and guard position at the end of each exchange type.
mindset.reset: If any marker is lost, take the shortest guarded step back to full stance.
mindset.anchor: Every exchange returns to balance.
mindset.context: Finish able to punch, kick, check or move immediately.

instructions: Review the athlete's recovery after a punch combination, kick and brief tie-up.
Identify the distinct balance error most common after each action.
Assign one small stance correction to each error.
progress: Track whether recovery completes before the next attack begins.

name: Scoring Route Decision (kickboxing)
why: Choose the opponent-specific route that produces clean legal scores rather than blocked activity.

mindset.intent: Build attacks toward the target their defence concedes most often.
mindset.focus: The expected guard, stance and distance after the matchup's opening action.
mindset.reset: If the route repeatedly meets full defence, exit and return to the alternative range.
mindset.anchor: Follow the defence to the open target.
mindset.context: Finish with a clean scoring strike and responsible stance recovery.

instructions: Review the expected opponent's defence to the planned opening weapon.
Trace the guard or weight reaction to the next available legal target.
Select one route and one blocked-route reset rather than adding volume.
progress: Grade the route by clean scores and balanced exits.

name: Exit Route Denial (kickboxing)
why: Deny the expected opponent's preferred exit after they finish attacking.

mindset.intent: Occupy the escape lane while remaining protected from their final strike.
mindset.focus: The lead-foot turn and shoulder direction at the end of their combination.
mindset.reset: If their final weapon still controls the lane, defend and hold centre instead of stepping through it.
mindset.anchor: Close the exit after the attack is truly over.
mindset.context: Finish facing the opponent with centre and stance retained.

instructions: Identify where the expected opponent moves after their primary combination.
Mark the final strike and foot turn that precede that exit.
Choose the safe lane-closing step and the active-weapon cue that delays it.
progress: Review whether route denial happens without entering the last strike.

name: Defensive Duty Check (kickboxing)
why: Attach the correct defensive responsibility to every matchup combination.

mindset.intent: Finish scoring sequences ready for the opponent's most likely return.
mindset.focus: The open side, planted leg or square stance left by the final planned strike.
mindset.reset: If recovery is late, shorten the combination and restore guard sooner.
mindset.anchor: The combination ends with defence.
mindset.context: Finish outside the expected return or structurally ready to block it.

instructions: List the opponent's likely punch, kick or knee return after each planned combination.
Identify which guard, check or exit the athlete must own on the final beat.
Remove the last strike if it prevents the defensive duty from being completed.
progress: Audit simulations for defended finishes, not combination length.

name: Opening Range Cue (kickboxing)
why: Retain one familiar signal for establishing the opening striking range.

mindset.intent: Use the trusted range action once and recover.
mindset.focus: The known opponent step that confirms the chosen distance.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: they cross range faster than expected; cover and take the practiced exit.
mindset.anchor: Set the range, keep the stance.
mindset.context: Finish in open space ready for the next legal weapon.

instructions: Name the single range cue retained from camp.
Pair it with the one familiar establishing action.
Close on the fast-crossing danger cue and known guarded exit.
progress: Use only this opening reminder during the taper.

name: Trusted Exit Cue (kickboxing)
why: Carry one proven exit cue into the final kickboxing review.

mindset.intent: Leave immediately when the familiar exchange-ending picture appears.
mindset.focus: The known foot or shoulder position that opens the safe lane.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the lane closes; cover in stance and use the practiced opposite reset.
mindset.anchor: See the lane, leave balanced.
mindset.context: Finish facing centre beyond the opponent's immediate return.

instructions: Recall the one exit picture confirmed in preparation.
Visualise the familiar step and guard recovery.
Name the closed-lane danger cue and the opposite reset.
progress: Keep the final rehearsal short and unchanged.

name: Neutral Decision Scan (combat-sport)
why: Identify one recurring opponent action that changes the next safe decision.

mindset.intent: Separate a reliable cue from background movement.
mindset.focus: The first repeatable movement immediately before the opponent commits.
mindset.reset: If it does not repeat, return to the athlete's established neutral position.
mindset.anchor: One repeated cue earns one rule.
mindset.context: Finish with a single observation that can be tested under the contest rules.

instructions: Review three comparable exchanges and record only the opponent's first committed movement.
Keep the cue only if it appears in more than one exchange.
Choose one familiar, rules-legal response and the position where it should finish.
progress: Confirm the cue once in the next scheduled technical session.

name: Neutral Trigger Response (combat-sport)
why: Match one opponent-specific trigger to a trained legal response.

mindset.intent: Act on the confirmed trigger without adding an unprepared second option.
mindset.focus: The exact posture, step or timing cue seen in matchup footage.
mindset.reset: If the picture differs, protect and return to the known starting position.
mindset.anchor: Exact trigger, trained answer.
mindset.context: Finish in the response's rehearsed safe position.

instructions: Name the expected opponent action and its earliest reliable trigger.
Pair it with the one response already established in training.
Define the different-picture cue that cancels the response and triggers reset.
progress: Test the trigger-response rule against varied opponent looks.

name: Neutral Opening Reminder (combat-sport)
why: Retain one familiar opening cue and response without new tactical analysis.

mindset.intent: Begin calmly and release the trained action only on the known cue.
mindset.focus: The single opening picture confirmed throughout preparation.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: the picture changes; protect and return to the practiced neutral reset.
mindset.anchor: Known cue, known action, safe finish.
mindset.context: Finish in the familiar position used after the opening response.

instructions: Name the one opening cue carried into competition.
Visualise the one trained response and its finishing position.
Close on the danger cue and the practiced reset.
progress: Keep this final reminder brief and unchanged.

name: Level Change Behind Pressure (MMA)
why: Choose the opponent-specific moment when forward striking hides the level change.

mindset.intent: Shoot beneath a committed defensive reaction, not beneath neutral posture.
mindset.focus: The planned strike making the opponent plant, shell or punch back with hips available.
mindset.reset: If their hips retreat or the entry line is visible, return to hands and recover the angle.
mindset.anchor: Hands make the level; the reaction makes the shot.
mindset.context: Finish on connected hips with head position or return safely to striking range.

instructions: Identify which pressure combination makes the expected opponent stop moving their feet.
Mark the beat where their guard commitment hides the change of level.
Define the failed-entry cue that sends the athlete back to striking rather than driving from poor position.
progress: Drill the strike-to-level timing against the expected reaction before adding a finish.

name: First Cage Decision (MMA)
why: Preload one familiar choice for the first time the opponent reaches the fence.

mindset.intent: Make the trained strike-or-connect decision without pausing at the boundary.
mindset.focus: The opponent's known guard and hip reaction on first fence contact.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: head position is lost; release, frame away and re-square in open space.
mindset.anchor: First fence touch, one clear branch.
mindset.context: Finish with effective offence or a clean reset, never passive fence holding.

instructions: Recall the single reaction that calls for continued striking.
Recall the alternative reaction that calls for immediate clinch connection.
Close with the known danger cue and one practiced disengagement.
progress: Keep this as a short first-contact rehearsal only.

name: Mat Return Cue (MMA)
why: Identify when the expected opponent's stand-up attempt exposes a safe mat return.

mindset.intent: Return them only while connection, head position and balance remain secure.
mindset.focus: Their posted hand leaving the floor, hips rising and weight committing to one foot.
mindset.reset: If grips slip or the opponent faces fully, release to stable clinch control rather than lifting from poor position.
mindset.anchor: Return the rising base, not a settled stance.
mindset.context: Finish above the hips in controlled top position ready to attack.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's preferred wall-walk or technical stand-up sequence.
Find the beat where one hand leaves support and their weight becomes returnable.
Choose the return direction and the grip-loss cue that cancels it.
progress: Drill the return from the opponent's real get-up timing and confirm top position afterwards.

name: Get-Up Denial (MMA)
why: Stop the expected opponent's preferred route back to standing before chasing secondary offence.

mindset.intent: Remove the post or hip angle that their get-up depends on.
mindset.focus: The first elbow, hand or knee they use to build height from bottom position.
mindset.reset: If the opponent clears the hips and faces up, reconnect safely or accept the standing reset.
mindset.anchor: Break the first post; preserve top position.
mindset.context: Finish with their shoulders or hips returned to the mat and a stable attacking base.

instructions: Classify whether the opponent builds up by wall-walk, underhook, sit-out or technical stand-up.
Identify the first support point that makes that route possible.
Choose the denial and the moment to switch from retention into effective offence.
progress: Review whether the first support was removed before the get-up gathered momentum.

name: Scramble Priority (MMA)
why: Choose the first positional objective when the expected transition becomes disordered.

mindset.intent: Secure the highest-value control before attacking during the scramble.
mindset.focus: Head height, hip line and which athlete has the first stable post.
mindset.reset: If no reliable post exists, protect the neck and hips while returning to base.
mindset.anchor: Post, hips, position, then offence.
mindset.context: Finish on top, behind the hips or safely disengaged with stance restored.

instructions: Study the scramble most likely to follow the primary takedown or escape exchange.
Rank the first objectives: protect submission danger, win head height, control hips, establish top.
Choose the opponent cue that changes the priority from control to disengagement.
progress: Rehearse the priority order from an unscripted transition and review the first decision only.

name: Cage Transition Choice (MMA)
why: Recognise how the cage changes the value of striking, clinch and takedown options.

mindset.intent: Choose the phase that uses the boundary without settling for empty control.
mindset.focus: Opponent foot position, underhook access and available striking angle at fence contact.
mindset.reset: If the boundary removes the planned offence, disengage to open space and rebuild.
mindset.anchor: Use the cage to create, not to pause.
mindset.context: Finish with a clean strike, advantageous connection or return to centre.

instructions: Review fence arrivals from striking and grappling entries separately.
Identify when the boundary opens a turn, takedown or safe striking lane.
Mark the neutral contact where leaving the cage is tactically superior.
progress: In situational work, require a productive decision within the first fence exchange.

name: Opponent Reaction to Phase Switch (MMA)
why: Use the expected opponent's strongest defence in one phase to enter the phase they protect least well.

mindset.intent: Switch on their committed defensive reaction rather than from impatience.
mindset.focus: The matchup-specific shell, sprawl, pummel or disengagement that overcommits posture.
mindset.reset: If the defence remains balanced, complete the current action and exit without forcing transition.
mindset.anchor: Committed defence opens the next phase.
mindset.context: Finish attacking where the opponent's recovery is weakest.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's best answer to the athlete's primary phase.
Locate what that answer concedes in distance, hand position, hips or stance.
Build the exact phase switch and the balanced-defence cue that cancels it.
progress: Rehearse the switch only against the correct opponent-specific reaction.

name: Pressure Reset (Kickboxing)
why: Recognise when forward movement loses punching and kicking balance.

mindset.intent: Pause the chase and restore a stance that can defend every legal return.
mindset.focus: Feet narrowing, shoulders leaning past the hips or the opponent gaining an outside angle.
mindset.reset: Step the hips back under the torso, rebuild guard and restart from centre.
mindset.anchor: Balanced feet make pressure dangerous.
mindset.context: Finish square to the opponent at the athlete's chosen entry range.

instructions: Find the first frame where pressure becomes reaching rather than ring cutting.
Name the foot or posture error and the opponent movement that caused it.
Choose one simple stance reset and one familiar feint to resume pressure.
progress: Use the reset before any new attack in the next pressure drill.

name: Body/Head Pressure Reaction (Kickboxing)
why: Exploit how the expected opponent moves their guard when pressure alternates body and head threats.

mindset.intent: Attack the level their defensive reaction leaves exposed.
mindset.focus: Elbows pinching, guard rising or torso folding after the planned body or head feint.
mindset.reset: If the guard stays compact and counters remain loaded, exit behind a low kick or angle.
mindset.anchor: Move the guard before choosing the level.
mindset.context: Finish with a clean score and guarded lateral exit.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's guard response to the selected body attack.
Map the head opening created by lowered elbows and the body opening created by a raised shell.
Define the compact-guard response that sends the athlete to the exit instead of forcing a target.
progress: Rehearse the level choice against randomised guard reactions.

name: Re-Catch After Exit (Kickboxing)
why: Predict where the expected opponent moves after escaping the first pressure exchange.

mindset.intent: Meet the second route while keeping defence ready for the exit counter.
mindset.focus: Whether they continue circling, reverse direction or plant to strike after gaining space.
mindset.reset: If the second cut enters a loaded counter line, hold centre and make them restart.
mindset.anchor: Read the escape after the escape.
mindset.context: Finish blocking the next lane with stance and guard intact.

instructions: Track the opponent's first movement immediately after a successful ring exit.
Place the second cut where that movement will arrive rather than following their path.
Name the shoulder or hip load that cancels the re-catch because a counter is prepared.
progress: Grade the next situational round on safe second cuts, not nonstop forward steps.

name: Opponent Entry Reaction (Kickboxing)
why: Learn the athlete's first safe response to different ways an opponent enters long range.

mindset.intent: Differentiate straight pressure, lateral entry and kick-led entry before acting.
mindset.focus: Lead-foot direction, hip load and whether hands or kicks initiate the approach.
mindset.reset: When the entry type is unclear, guard and move to open space before countering.
mindset.anchor: Classify the entry before choosing the answer.
mindset.context: Finish at long range with the opponent's forward line broken.

instructions: Collect examples of straight, angled and kick-led entries.
Assign a long weapon, defensive step or guarded exit to each entry type.
Name the ambiguous cue that requires movement without a counter.
progress: Call the entry type correctly during the next range drill.

name: Ring Position Warning Cue (Kickboxing)
why: Recognise the opponent-specific warning that long-range retreat is approaching the boundary.

mindset.intent: Turn toward centre before the expected pressure pattern removes both exits.
mindset.focus: The boundary marker plus the opponent's shoulder line and second advancing step.
mindset.reset: If the warning is missed, cover, step across their lead side and rebuild long range.
mindset.anchor: See the boundary before feeling it.
mindset.context: Finish facing centre with room to kick and pivot on both sides.

instructions: Trace where the expected opponent's pressure line usually meets the ring boundary.
Choose the visual floor or post marker that signals the final safe turn.
Attach the early centre exit and a separate late-contact escape.
progress: Review whether the warning cue triggers movement before stance narrows.

name: Opponent Tie-Up Response (Kickboxing)
why: Prepare for how the expected opponent reacts when brief close-range contact is made.

mindset.intent: Choose immediate knee, frame-and-strike or release from their first response.
mindset.focus: Whether they stiff-arm, cover, turn, posture tall or drive chest-to-chest.
mindset.reset: If contact becomes static, obey the break and return to stance without fighting for prolonged control.
mindset.anchor: First response decides the one legal action.
mindset.context: Finish after a prompt score or clean separation with guard restored.

instructions: Catalogue the expected opponent's first reaction to upper-body contact.
Match open torso, hard frame and turning escape to distinct rule-appropriate responses.
Define the static-contact cue that ends the exchange immediately.
progress: Rehearse random responses with one action maximum before release.

name: Range Boundary Scan (combat-sport)
why: Recognise where the opponent first becomes able to score under the applicable rules.

mindset.intent: Respect the true scoring boundary without giving away unnecessary space.
mindset.focus: The opponent's lead step or posture change as they enter effective range.
mindset.reset: If distance becomes uncertain, return to the athlete's trained outside marker.
mindset.anchor: Know when the contest becomes live.
mindset.context: Finish at a distance where the next legal action remains visible.

instructions: Mark the first frame where the opponent can reach with a valid scoring action.
Compare that boundary with the athlete's preferred working distance.
Choose the familiar step or guard change used when the boundary is crossed.
progress: Check the marker in technical practice without introducing a new technique.

name: Rhythm Pause Map (combat-sport)
why: Find the repeated pause between the opponent's actions and their reset.

mindset.intent: Use timing information without assuming every pause is an opening.
mindset.focus: The beat where their feet, guard or posture stop moving together.
mindset.reset: If tempo changes, defend and restart the rhythm count.
mindset.anchor: Count the reset, not just the attack.
mindset.context: Finish with one repeatable timing window and one no-window condition.

instructions: Count three complete opponent sequences from start through reset.
Mark the pause that appears in the same place more than once.
Choose one familiar legal action that fits inside that pause.
progress: Validate the timing in the next scheduled technical round.

name: Defensive Recovery Audit (combat-sport)
why: See what defensive responsibility remains after the athlete completes an action.

mindset.intent: Restore guard, stance or position before beginning again.
mindset.focus: The first exposed line or loss of balance at the end of the exchange.
mindset.reset: If recovery is incomplete, shorten the action and return to structure.
mindset.anchor: Recovery closes the exchange.
mindset.context: Finish in the athlete's established defensible position.

instructions: Review three athlete actions through the final recovery beat.
Identify the guard, base or positional duty left incomplete after each.
Select the smallest familiar correction that closes the exposure.
progress: Track complete recoveries rather than total actions in practice.

name: Preferred Exit Map (combat-sport)
why: Identify where the opponent most often moves after an exchange ends.

mindset.intent: Recognise their preferred exit before deciding whether to follow or hold position.
mindset.focus: The first foot and body direction used after their final action.
mindset.reset: If the exit varies, keep the athlete's established central or neutral position.
mindset.anchor: Read the departure before choosing pursuit.
mindset.context: Finish with one confirmed exit tendency and a safe observation position.

instructions: Collect comparable exchanges that end without interruption.
Record the opponent's first movement after their final legal action.
Keep only the direction that repeats and name the safe response to it.
progress: Confirm the exit tendency once under technical conditions.

name: Balance Warning Cue (combat-sport)
why: Recognise the athlete's earliest sign that tactical action is losing physical structure.

mindset.intent: Stop adding offence once balance or base no longer supports defence.
mindset.focus: Head passing the base, feet narrowing or posture turning away from the opponent.
mindset.reset: Return weight under the body and rebuild the familiar guard or position.
mindset.anchor: Structure authorises the next action.
mindset.context: Finish balanced and able to respond in either direction.

instructions: Freeze examples at the first loss of stance, base or aligned posture.
Identify which tactical choice most often produces that warning.
Choose one familiar structural reset before any renewed action.
progress: Use the warning cue once in practice and verify an immediate reset.

name: Safe Reset Route (combat-sport)
why: Define how the athlete returns to a known position after an exchange becomes unclear.

mindset.intent: Reset through the safest available route instead of pausing in uncertainty.
mindset.focus: The opponent line and open space available when structure is lost.
mindset.reset: If the preferred route closes, protect first and use the trained secondary reset.
mindset.anchor: Unclear exchange, clear route home.
mindset.context: Finish in the athlete's established neutral position with the opponent visible.

instructions: Review moments where the athlete loses the intended tactical picture.
Identify the safest route back to known distance, stance or control.
Name the closed-route cue and the secondary protective reset.
progress: Rehearse the return route without adding a counterattack.

name: Second Decision Branch (combat-sport)
why: Prepare the next choice after the expected opponent answers the first action.

mindset.intent: Make the second decision from their actual reaction, not from a memorised sequence.
mindset.focus: The matchup-specific posture or direction immediately after the opening response.
mindset.reset: If the reaction is unfamiliar, finish safely and reset the exchange.
mindset.anchor: First action asks; second action answers.
mindset.context: Finish the branch in a trained scoring or control position.

instructions: Choose the planned first action and the opponent's two most likely responses.
Assign a distinct familiar continuation to each expected response.
Define the unfamiliar response that ends the branch.
progress: Rehearse the second choice with randomised expected reactions.

name: Preferred Route Denial (combat-sport)
why: Remove the expected opponent's most reliable route to a scoring position.

mindset.intent: Deny the route at its earliest visible gate.
mindset.focus: The step, posture or contact that begins their preferred sequence.
mindset.reset: If denial is late, protect the threatened line and exit the sequence.
mindset.anchor: Close the first gate, not the final door.
mindset.context: Finish outside the opponent's preferred route with structure intact.

instructions: Trace the opponent's highest-value sequence backward from its finish.
Identify the earliest legal and repeatable point of denial.
Choose the early denial and a separate late-read safety response.
progress: Review whether practice stops the route before its strongest action.

name: Score-and-Exit Rule (combat-sport)
why: Attach an opponent-specific safe finish to the athlete's primary scoring action.

mindset.intent: Leave the expected return line as part of the score.
mindset.focus: The opponent's first recovery movement after the selected legal action lands.
mindset.reset: If the exit lane closes, protect in place and use the trained alternate route.
mindset.anchor: The score is complete when position is safe.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the expected return with balance restored.

instructions: Identify the opponent's most likely answer to the athlete's primary score.
Choose the exit direction that makes that answer turn or fall short.
Add the blocked-lane cue and familiar alternate reset.
progress: Grade the score and exit as one complete tactical action.

name: Momentum Adjustment (combat-sport)
why: Recognise when the opponent changes pace after success or adversity.

mindset.intent: Adjust distance or timing before matching their new intensity.
mindset.focus: A sudden reduction or increase in the gap between their committed actions.
mindset.reset: If the pace change is uncertain, protect and gather one more exchange.
mindset.anchor: Change position before changing output.
mindset.context: Finish with the athlete operating from a controllable tempo and position.

instructions: Review how the expected opponent behaves immediately after winning and losing exchanges.
Identify the pace cue that reliably marks their momentum change.
Choose one familiar spacing or timing adjustment for that cue.
progress: Test the adjustment without escalating output automatically.

name: Late-Round Choice (combat-sport)
why: Prepare one disciplined decision for the opponent's late-round pattern.

mindset.intent: Choose control, score or reset from the actual position rather than the clock alone.
mindset.focus: The expected opponent's posture and pace in the final exchange window.
mindset.reset: If the athlete's structure fades, protect position and avoid a forced finish.
mindset.anchor: Late does not mean reckless.
mindset.context: Finish the round in a scoring or clearly defensible position.

instructions: Study the expected opponent's final exchanges in comparable rounds.
Identify whether they surge, protect, stall or lose structure.
Assign one familiar response and the fatigue cue that overrides it for safety.
progress: Rehearse the decision from realistic late-round posture.

name: Corner Cue Translation (combat-sport)
why: Turn one expected corner instruction into a precise in-contest action.

mindset.intent: Connect short language to a trained cue, response and finish.
mindset.focus: The exact visual or positional picture the corner phrase refers to.
mindset.reset: If the picture is absent, stay with the current safe plan rather than forcing the instruction.
mindset.anchor: Hear the words, find the picture.
mindset.context: Finish in the position the instruction was designed to create.

instructions: Choose one likely corner phrase for the matchup.
Define the opponent cue and familiar response represented by that phrase.
Name the absent-picture condition that keeps the athlete on the current plan.
progress: Practice receiving the phrase between short tactical scenarios.

name: Opening Test Adjustment (combat-sport)
why: Use one safe opening action to confirm or reject a matchup assumption.

mindset.intent: Gather information with a familiar action and adjust only from the observed result.
mindset.focus: The expected opponent response to the preselected opening test.
mindset.reset: If the response is different, return to neutral and delay the adjustment.
mindset.anchor: Test once, observe fully, then decide.
mindset.context: Finish the opening test in a safe position with a clear next rule.

instructions: Name the matchup assumption that the opening action is meant to test.
Define the expected response and the one familiar adjustment it authorises.
Define the unexpected response that triggers reset and further observation.
progress: Rehearse the test without turning it into a fixed combination.

name: Danger Cue Override (combat-sport)
why: Give one opponent-specific danger cue authority to cancel the planned attack.

mindset.intent: Protect position immediately when the known high-risk picture appears.
mindset.focus: The exact stance, posture or timing signal preceding the opponent's best threat.
mindset.reset: Use the trained defensive reset and restart only after the picture clears.
mindset.anchor: Danger cue overrides the plan.
mindset.context: Finish beyond the threat line in the athlete's familiar structure.

instructions: Identify the expected opponent's highest-consequence action.
Rewind to the earliest reliable cue that announces it.
Attach one defensive response and the condition for safely restarting offence.
progress: Test whether the athlete cancels the plan before the danger action develops.

name: Familiar Reset Reminder (combat-sport)
why: Keep one trained reset available if the opening exchange becomes unfamiliar.

mindset.intent: Protect first and return directly to the established neutral position.
mindset.focus: The single known sign that stance, base or tactical structure has broken.
mindset.reset: Danger cue: attempting a new solution; use the practiced reset instead.
mindset.anchor: Nothing new; return to what is trained.
mindset.context: Finish balanced in the familiar neutral position.

instructions: Recall the one loss-of-structure cue used during camp.
Visualise the single practiced reset attached to it.
Name the temptation to improvise and replace it with the known response.
progress: End the review after one clear mental repetition.
